stores.name: Editable SQLite
stores.description: CRUD store; app-level roles; corrections and dispute status updated in place

storage.method: SQLite page_count×page_size ÷ records (after WAL checkpoint); evidence files excluded for all stores

stores.name: Hardened SQLite
stores.description: Append-only triggers; SHA-256 hash chain; app-level roles

storage.method: SQLite page_count×page_size ÷ records (after WAL checkpoint); evidence files excluded for all stores

stores.name: Hardened + checkpoints
stores.description: As hardened, plus head hashes handed to an independent party after every write

storage.method: SQLite page_count×page_size ÷ records (after WAL checkpoint); evidence files excluded for all stores

stores.name: PatchLedger (local chain)
stores.description: Solidity contract enforces roles and append-only links; payloads off-chain, digests on-chain

storage.method: off-chain: SQLite page_count×page_size ÷ records; on-chain: contract storage slots written (4×32 B per record + per-device and per-correction mapping slots), from the struct layout

scenarios.title: Unauthorized modification of an existing record
scenarios.attacker: Database administrator edits a claim directly (bypassing the app) and recomputes that record's own digest/hash

editable.note: No integrity metadata covers record content

hardened.note: Edits of the newest record leave no broken link and pass local verification

scenarios.title: Consistent history rewrite
scenarios.attacker: Database administrator edits a claim and recomputes every subsequent hash so the local chain is self-consistent

hardened-anchored.note: Detected because the externally held head hash no longer matches

blockchain.note: Off-chain rewrite detected; the on-chain rewrite attempt reverted (StalePrevHash)

scenarios.title: Deletion of an event record
scenarios.attacker: Database administrator deletes a record row

editable.note: Only deletions that leave a sequence gap are noticed; deleting the newest record is not

hardened.note: Deleting the newest record leaves the remaining chain valid

scenarios.title: Alteration of a supporting evidence file
scenarios.attacker: Attacker with write access to the evidence file store replaces a file's bytes

editable.note: Detected because this baseline also stores SHA-256 digests

scenarios.title: Evidence file and its stored digest replaced together
scenarios.attacker: Attacker with database and file-store access replaces a file and updates the digest stored with it (recomputing that record's own hash where one exists)

scenarios.title: Unauthorized role submits a record
scenarios.attacker: A party without the required role (buyer, auditor, unregistered account, or a different repairer correcting someone else's claim) uses the normal write path

editable.note: Rejected by application code; relies on every write going through the application

scenarios.title: Insider forges a record in an authorized party's name
scenarios.attacker: Operator of the record store inserts a well-formed repair record attributed to an authorized repairer, without that repairer's key

hardened.note: Hash chains without per-party signatures cannot attribute records; the forged record is correctly hashed

blockchain.note: The insider lacks the repairer's key, so the transaction reverts; an off-chain-only row is flagged UNANCHORED_RECORD

scenarios.title: Attempt to hide or overwrite an unresolved dispute
scenarios.attacker: A buyer's challenge is open; the record-store operator tries to make it disappear (status edit, forged resolution, or deletion)

editable.note: Dispute status is an editable column

hardened.note: A correctly hashed resolution forged in the auditor's name is indistinguishable from a real one

blockchain.note: Non-auditor resolution reverts; open-dispute state lives in the contract; deleting the off-chain copy is flagged

scenarios.title: Reuse of a previously submitted evidence digest
scenarios.attacker: A byte-identical receipt is submitted again for a different device

editable.note: Same digest-lookup query in every store: an analysis feature, not a blockchain property

scenarios.title: Conflicting claims about a component replacement
scenarios.attacker: One repairer records a battery replacement; a later inspection asserts the original battery

scenarios.title: Correction preserves the earlier claim
scenarios.attacker: The original author corrects a claim through the normal write path; is the original wording still retrievable?

editable.note: Conventional CRUD correction overwrites the claim in place

blockchain.note: Correction is a new record; the original is unchanged on- and off-chain

notes: Measured directly: insert latency (one record, application path, excluding evidence-file upload), full-history verification latency per device, throughput (records ÷ summed insert time, single sequential client), SQLite size, gas and calldata from transaction receipts.

Simulated: attack outcomes. Each attack is actually executed against the store, then that store's own verifier is run. P = prevented (the operation was rejected), D = applied but detected, U = applied and not detected.

The local Hardhat chain automines every transaction instantly on one node; real deployments add block/consensus latency (seconds) and replication. Latencies here are lower bounds for the blockchain design.
Blockchain verification includes RPC reads of the on-chain records and re-hashing of evidence files, so it is not directly comparable to an in-process SQLite scan.
On-chain bytes per record are computed from the contract's storage layout, not measured from node disk usage.

Insider model: the attacker controls the off-chain database and file store but not other parties' signing keys. In this prototype the server holds all demo keys for convenience, which a production deployment must not do.

The hardened baseline with external checkpoints detects rewrites of already-checkpointed history as well as the blockchain does; its remaining gap is attribution (no per-party signatures) and the operator's ability to append records in others' names.
Single run on one machine; results are descriptive. No statistical significance testing was performed; repeat with several seeds to assess variability.
